name: Ceftizoxime

overview.mechanism: A beta-lactam antibacterial acting through inhibition of bacterial cell-wall synthesis.
uses: Treatment of susceptible bacterial infections; consult the current Philippine insert for indication-specific doses.

paragraphs.text: A 20-participant study found a strong relationship between ceftizoxime clearance and creatinine clearance. Mean half-life was markedly longer with very low kidney function; a four-hour hemodialysis session reduced serum concentrations by about 52%.

Dialysis removal in this historical study is not evidence that an unadjusted dose is safe or that all modern dialysis prescriptions are equivalent. Product-label dosing and the actual dialysis prescription remain necessary.

evidence.title: Historical US label: kidney and safety precautions

paragraphs.text: The August 2007 Cefizox label requires renal maintenance-dose modification after an initial 500 mg–1 g IM or IV dose. Its table uses creatinine clearance in mL/min and separates less severe from life-threatening infections; the serum creatinine used for estimation should reflect steady-state renal function.

For hemodialysis, that label times the scheduled dose at the end of dialysis and states that a separate supplemental dose is unnecessary. This is historical product labeling, not a modern CRRT or peritoneal-dialysis regimen or confirmation of the Philippine product's instructions.

The label advises renal assessment, particularly in seriously ill patients receiving maximum doses. It describes cephalosporin-associated seizures especially with renal impairment and unreduced dosing, and recommends prothrombin-time monitoring in patients at risk of reduced prothrombin activity, including renal or hepatic impairment, poor nutrition, prolonged therapy, or anticoagulant use.
